---
title: "unnest() drops the rows whose list is empty"
ref: TDY-09
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "customers b and c kept, with NA"
versions: "All versions of {tidyr}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022)"
---

::: {.piege packages="tidyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyr))

orders <- tibble(
  customer = c("a", "b", "c"),
  items = list(1:2, NULL, integer())
)
unnest(orders, cols = items)
```
:::

## Why

`unnest()` creates one row per element of each list. A `NULL` or zero-length list contains no element: it produces no row, and the customer vanishes from the result. Nothing flags the loss.

Any counts made afterwards (number of customers, share of customers without an order) are then wrong, since the customers without items no longer exist.

## The fix

`keep_empty = TRUE` keeps a row with `NA` for each empty list.

::: {.piege packages="tidyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyr))

unnest(orders, cols = items, keep_empty = TRUE)
```
:::
